newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary parliament allows tripling of soc sec gap.
newsitem.headline: Hungary parliament allows tripling of soc sec gap.

text.p: BUDAPEST, Nov 26 (REUTER) - Hungary's parliament late on Tuesday passed a budget amendment allowing a 1996 social security deficit of 60.1 billion forints, over three times the original target, Wednesday's Magyar Hirlap reported.

The government set a social security deficit target of 17.8 billion forints in March as part of a package of measures agreed with the International Monetary Fund aimed at ensuring a 1996 government budget deficit of no more than four percent of gross domestic prodict.

The Finance Ministry announced earlier this month that the deficit had widened to 62.2 billion forints in September from 56 billion forints at the end of August but added the higher gap was unlikely to threaten the four-per-cent target as customs and tax revenues would be higher than planned.
Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy recently said that without new measures the gap could reach 80 billion forints next year.
Hungary's Welfare Minister Gyorgy Szabo resigned earlier this week over differences with the Finance Ministry over the health care funding for 1997.
He added that the institutions in the system would need 270 billion forints for their operations in 1997, but next year's budget would only provide them with 258.5 billion forints.
